overview: Finalize the deep-mantle simulation by implementing deterministic state compression for long-running campaigns and optimizing the Monte Carlo convergence logic for endgame stability. This batch closes the final coverage gaps in simulation persistence and statistical validation.

tasks.title: Deterministic State Compression for 5k+ Tick Campaigns
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a zero-heap, stack-based compression algorithm for the simulation state vector. Use C++20 concepts to constrain template parameters. The algorithm must process the 16,500-step history into a fixed-size 256-byte checksum plus a sparse delta map. No dynamic allocations allowed. Use std::array for all buffers. Ensure deterministic iteration order for reproducible checksums.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic output verified across 100 Monte Carlo runs.
Compilation time < 2 seconds for the header.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Faster save/load times and smaller save files for long campaigns, improving overall responsiveness.

tasks.title: Optimized Monte Carlo Convergence Check for Endgame
tasks.architectural_spec: Refactor the Monte Carlo convergence check to use a fixed-point arithmetic approach for stability. Implement a 3-stage convergence detector: 1) Variance check, 2) Mean drift check, 3) Final state lock. Use constexpr functions for the threshold values. The logic must fit within 40 lines of code, leveraging C++20 structured bindings for result unpacking.
acceptance_criteria: Convergence detected within 10 iterations for stable states.
No floating-point non-determinism in final state.
Unit tests pass for 100% survival rate scenarios.
tasks.player_fun_impact: More reliable and faster endgame calculations, reducing perceived lag during campaign completion.
